// diagnostic E0773

Jet.CrossedArgumentNames

A positional argument is named like a different parameter of the same type

What

A positional argument is named like a different parameter of the same type

Why

Passing a variable by position when its name matches another parameter of the same type usually means the arguments were swapped

Fix

Swap the arguments to match the declaration order, or label them explicitly.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning Jet.CrossedArgumentNames: Tests/UI/crossed_argument_names.stderr.

Error: Jet.CrossedArgumentNames: Arguments `dst` and `src` are crossed in this call to `copy_pair`
  --> Tests/UI/crossed_argument_names.jet:8:18
    |
  8 |     _: copy_pair(dst, src)
    |                  ^^^^^^^^
 Why: `copy_pair` declares `src` before `dst` with the same type `String`, so passing `(dst, src)` by position looks swapped
 Fix: Reorder them to `(src, dst)`, or label them explicitly as `src: dst, dst: src`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/Jet.CrossedArgumentNames

Error: Jet.CrossedArgumentNames: Arguments `(b, c, a)` are crossed in this call to `rotate`
  --> Tests/UI/crossed_argument_names.jet:13:15
    |
 13 |     _: rotate(b, c, a)
    |               ^^^^^^^
 Why: `rotate` declares `(a, b, c)` with the same type `Int`, so passing `(b, c, a)` by position looks rotated
 Fix: Reorder them to `(a, b, c)`, or label them explicitly as `a: b, b: c, c: a`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/Jet.CrossedArgumentNames
